newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures stuck in sideways trade.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures stuck in sideways trade.

text.p: German debt traded sideways at higher levels late on Monday as both U.S. Treasury market gains and a sense Germany's economic recovery is still sputtering supported the market.
Despite the gains, however, dealers were sceptical resistance levels could be broken in the coming days and instead predicted more range-trading at higher levels.
"I think we will see more range-trading with a bias to the upside," a Frankfurt dealer said.
The March Bund futures contract, traded on Frankfurt's DTB exchange was at 101.82, up 10 basis points at 1517 GMT.
At the same time, the benchmark cash bond maturing January 2007 was trading at 102.06 compared with Friday's 102.02 close.

The market took comfort from lower-than-expected U.S. purchasing mangager data, indicating low inflationary risks. The January NAPM index showed a drop to 52.0 from December's 54.0 figure. This was below the 53.0 number that was expected.
But the German market's reaction was less exuberant than U.S. Treasury price increases. "Treasuries liked the data, but this has not fully come through to us," another dealer said.
Looking ahead, dealers are more confident U.S. rates will remain steady in light of moderate inflationary pressures.
In Germany the market is also eyeing a slew of economic data scheduled for release this week and the Bundesbank's regularly scheduled policy-setting meeting on Thursday.
Dealers largely expect the economic data, particularly January unemployment statistics to be released on Thursday, to show a still struggling economy.

On the other hand hopes for any sort of German interest rate reduction have largely been swept out of the market by a succession of Bundesbank officials' comments that there is no need for another reduction now. The Bundesbank has often said the economy has sufficient liquidity to recover.

Additionally the week may be overshadowed by the upcoming G7 meeting in Berlin where finance ministers and central bankers are expected to address currency market concerns, particularly the dollar's recent sharp increase.
Dealers said there were currently too many variables at play that it would difficult to predict anything but range-trade at higher levels.
Resistance is still seen at around 101.92 while first support levels are around 101.66.
